steps.content: A brief pause in the skirmish reveals Christina's numerous injuries, yet she hasn't even managed to touch the woman's hair. The enemy's strength far exceeds expectations.
She watches Christina, who is now panting heavily.

steps.speaker: Suspect
steps.content: I thought a specially dispatched Sinner detective would be more capable. You're quite the disappointment, young missy.

steps.speaker: Christina
steps.content: Hmph, I couldn't care less about your opinion.
While talking tough, Christina secretly observes the weapon in the woman's hand.
It's a crimson crystallized dagger, drawn from thin air, adorned with a few strange flowers—the same as the Mania Flower found on the victim, Anania.

steps.speaker: Christina
steps.content: I knew it was you. Must be my lucky day to catch the real culprit so quickly.

steps.speaker: Christina
steps.content: You left the crime scene in such an extravagant state, flaunting your Mania abilities. Were you taunting us? Or were you hoping to be praised by others?

steps.speaker: Christina
steps.content: Ha, you're a show-off and a narcissist, thinking everyone in the world will dance to your tune. You were fooling us over the phone while admiring your own performance art up close... Hmph, too bad you ran into me!

steps.speaker: Christina
steps.content: Let me, the <size=25><color=#7683a2>future</color></size> great detective Christina, show you what a real setback looks like.

steps.speaker: Suspect
steps.content: Heh, did they teach you profiling in your first year of school? That answer is passable, I guess.

steps.speaker: Suspect
steps.content: But you're a bit slow, silly girl. I've been giving you clues since my first sentence to you.

steps.speaker: Suspect
steps.content: Hello there, rookie detective.

steps.speaker: Suspect
steps.content: The experienced inspector knew the scene was being watched the moment he heard that. He searched for suspects carefully and discreetly without causing a stir. And you? You were 47 seconds late and shouting like an imbecile.

steps.speaker: Christina
steps.content: Well... I don't need you lecturing me! Come with me, confess everything, tell us how and why you committed these crimes, and whether you had accomplices.

steps.speaker: Christina
steps.content: You said Anania isn't dead, that you turned her into a flower. Can she still be saved?

steps.speaker: Christina
steps.content: Remove your ability! Right now, you're only guilty of assault and will be supervised in MBCC. But if you cross that line, you'll be a murderer, and trampling on life is an unforgivable crime! You—

steps.speaker: Suspect
steps.content: Hahahaha!

steps.speaker: Suspect
steps.content: Ha... nothing, just thought of something funny. It's been a while since I've seen someone like you...
Without blinking, Christina watches as the woman disappears before her eyes. Then, the woman's voice sounds from behind her.

steps.speaker: Suspect
steps.content: ...Such an overly righteous fool.

Christina doesn't have time to react. The woman's hand is already around her neck from behind. Her fingertips lightly touch Christina's chin, tracing the curve of her throat downwards. Suddenly, Christina feels a strange numbness as something is drawn out from within her.

steps.speaker: Suspect
steps.content: You dare to insult me, thinking I'm as useless as you, a complete novice?

steps.speaker: Suspect
steps.content: ...The word "murderer" can't define me, detective. The "life" and "justice" we see are different.
Her hand continues to move outwards, pulling out a budding crimson flower. The bud bursts out from Christina's chest, slowly stretching upwards.

steps.speaker: Suspect
steps.content: Look, people can <color=#fb9259>bloom</color>. This is your flower, take good care of it. Hurting it is the same as hurting yourself.

steps.speaker: Suspect
steps.content: I believe life is precious. Even the most ugly and despicable person can bloom beautiful flowers. The body and soul will become nutrients, nourishing the flower until it blooms. Only then is it a truly pure <color=#fb9259>life</color>.

steps.speaker: Suspect
steps.content: Yours looks like a naive and cute little flower. A sunflower? Or a daisy?

The crimson bud sprouts, slowly unfolding. A wave of nausea rises within Christina as if her blood is being drawn from the ends of her vessels. She musters all her strength to squeeze out a question through her teeth.

steps.speaker: Christina
steps.content: What... happens when the flower... fully blooms?

steps.speaker: Suspect
steps.content: It will keep going, blooming more and more flowers, just like the woman in the water, until she can't bear any more.

steps.speaker: Suspect
steps.content: Life is powerful, the stronger the person, the more they can bear. I've seen someone bloom an entire Garden.

steps.speaker: Christina
steps.content: I asked... what happens to those who have <color=#fb9259>"bloomed"</color>, after their life has been drained?

steps.speaker: Suspect
steps.content: Oh, that's what you meant.
A smile shows on her face.

steps.speaker: Suspect
steps.content: When you're admiring a flower, do you care about the mud under your feet?

steps.speaker: Christina
steps.content: You bastard!!

Fury surges within Christina, her hatred overcoming her fear and allowing her to reclaim control of her body. Ignoring the threat, she spins around and swings at the woman, who easily dodges. Christina then throws her cane towards where the woman retreated.
Boom—!!

steps.speaker: Christina
steps.content: That's someone's life, what right do you have to distort and trample it?!
The wall is shattered by the thrown cane, dust fills the alley. The punctured sheriff's hat falls pathetically, the woman's figure vaguely visible through the dust.
Her long hair floats around her, a deep red flower in her hand. She seems very pleased.

steps.speaker: Suspect
steps.content: You got mad, huh? Hahaha, I'd say this is much more beautiful than your boring "justice."

Christina's cane is still stuck in the wall behind the enemy. The strength she used in that strike has left her drained, or perhaps—having her "flower" plucked has indeed robbed her of some life force. It's now very difficult for her to move, she grits her teeth in fury.

steps.speaker: Christina
steps.content: Shut up, bastard. I remember now.

steps.speaker: Christina
steps.content: July, at Erica Villa, the sheriffs had their lives drained by a Sinner. Rahu said that a <color=#fb9259>crimson thorn</color> was left at the scene.

steps.speaker: Christina
steps.content: You're the one who attacked Erica Villa, who attacked Shalom! You're the leader of the Garden Sinners, the <color=#fb9259>Mentor</color> of assassins!
The "Mentor" laughs even more.

steps.speaker: Suspect
steps.content: Shalom, huh... Are you really that fond of her? Hehe...

steps.speaker: Suspect
steps.content: Perfect, then you should play with <color=#fb9259>me</color> too.

steps.speaker: Christina
steps.content: I don't have time to play with you, I'm going to—ahhh!
A white blade plunges straight into Christina's left leg. She kneels in pain, completely losing the ability to move.
Upon removal, the white blade turns out to be just an ordinary note. There are a few lines of small characters inside.

In garden deep, where spring blossoms dive, 
emerald waters their whispers abide.
On a night of rains, fireflies glide; 
by fractured walls, shadows of ruins reside.

In autumn's prime, wine and meat gleam. 
Gold and silver set the festive scene.
As year's end nears, vast and wide, 
over dried-up wells, I alone stride.

steps.speaker: Christina
steps.content: Where spring blossoms dive... Could this be... <color=#fb9259>an assassination warning</color>? So this isn't the only case, are you planning to...!!

steps.speaker: Suspect
steps.content: Mm-hmm, this is just the beginning. I made a promise for a grand bloom, and I will keep my word.

steps.speaker: Suspect
steps.content: When and where the next flower will bloom, and for what reason... Why don't you deduce? The future great detective Christina, treat it like your favorite detective game.

steps.speaker: Suspect
steps.content: If you can solve my riddles, I'll accept a commission from you. Any person you want me to kill, save, or spare, I'll listen to you. But if you can't solve them...

steps.speaker: Suspect
steps.content: You, your Shalom, the ones you love, many people will turn into blooming flowers, to decorate my <color=#fb9259>Garden</color>.

steps.speaker: Christina
steps.content: You—?!

steps.speaker: Suspect
steps.content: Alright, alright, get moving. If you have time to be angry with me here, the second flower might have already bloomed.

steps.speaker: Christina
steps.content: The second... Could it be?!

steps.speaker: Christina
steps.content: Look, I've found the first suspect! The owner of this suspicious phone number is a 48-year-old male called <color=#fb9259>Nathan</color>. The file says he's an Eastsider, but his past is very suspicious. Please allow me to keep investigating!

The woman takes a luxurious phone out of her pocket, waves it around, and throws it at Christina's face. Christina quickly catches it. The phone screen is already shattered, and her intuition tells her that this is Nathan's phone.

steps.speaker: Suspect
steps.content: Figure it out yourself, it's best to bring more people, your talk of justice alone can't stop me.

steps.speaker: Suspect
steps.content: By the way, here you go, little detective. This is your flower.
She gently lets go, and the flower pulled out from Christina's body falls to the ground. It's a tender flower that looks like a daisy or a sunflower, Christina couldn't recognize it.

steps.speaker: Suspect
steps.content: Marigold isn't known to be sunny, so don't force yourself to play the role of a justice hero. Challenge me with your true self, then I might be able to expect something from you.

steps.speaker: Suspect
steps.content: This is a blooming period that has been brewing for <color=#fb9259>10 years</color>. I've lowered the difficulty for you, you better win.

steps.speaker: Christina
steps.content: 10 years... what does that mean... What happened in <color=#fb9259>103</color>?

She doesn't respond, laughing loudly as she turns around and leaves. Christina wants to chase after her, but her body is blooming and injured, no longer listening to her commands. All she can do is yell at the figure that's leaving.

steps.speaker: Christina
steps.content: Don't run!! You bastard, what did that mean just now?!

steps.speaker: Christina
steps.content: What does the case have to do with N.F. 103?
The further investigation of the case quickly yields results.

Intelligence Department: Regarding the other "flowers that shouldn't have been present" at the scene, we understand the reason for their presence. Central Park doesn't have <color=#fb9259>Daisies</color>, which only bloom in spring. The Intelligence Department has searched the entire Eastside and finally found something interesting.


Intelligence Department: Back in the <color=#fb9259>spring of N.F. 104</color>, a woman drowned here. The investigation ruled out homicide, but the photos from the crime scene at that time are quite interesting.

Christina: The posture, layout, and daisies at the scene are very similar to the Anania case. What's the connection between these two people?


Intelligence Department: There's no concrete evidence yet, but they're definitely related to one thing.


Intelligence Department: The famous FAC <color=#fb9259>debacle</color> in N.F. 103.

Intelligence Department: The deceased is named Ophelia, originally from the FAC Communications Department, and had participated in supporting a major operation in N.F. 103.


Intelligence Department: We haven't yet applied for enough permissions to query the details, but we do know that the operation seems to have suffered a major defeat, with heavy casualties. This triggered a series of chain reactions, including several people in charge, and the then commander of FAC, taking the blame and resigning. The former commander died of illness soon after.


Intelligence Department: Although Ophelia was not in a high position, she also left the FAC at the beginning of N.F. 104 due to physical and mental illness. Three months later, she was found drowned in a pond.

Intelligence Department: As for Anania, she was not a member of FAC. But she was in charge of handling the <color=#fb9259>internal publicity crisis of FAC</color> in N.F. 103, and the several articles she published stated that the defeat in N.F. 103 was due to the internal intelligence and communications personnel, which involved Ophelia.


Intelligence Department: This caused quite a stir at the time...
